skill.name: copywriting
skill.description: Creates clear, honest marketing copy for homepages, landing pages, pricing pages, feature pages, product pages, and about pages.
skill.summary: Builds structured conversion copy from a confirmed brief, with alternatives and testing guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The four static findings are false positives caused by ordinary copywriting guidance. The skill contains no code, tool calls, network access, filesystem access, credential handling, or prompt injection aimed at bypassing review.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid buzzwords unless customers use them
Avoid stacking features without narrative flow.
- Avoid combining multiple messages into one element

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 117 is a copy style rule about avoiding buzzwords unless customers use them. It does not request system inspection, environment discovery, or host reconnaissance.
Line 155 advises narrative flow in marketing copy. It contains no instruction to inspect system settings, files, processes, or local configuration.
Line 191 is testability guidance for writing focused headlines and CTAs. It does not ask the agent to gather host, network, or security information.
Line 32 says clarity beats cleverness as a writing principle. There is no network probing, connectivity testing, or external target discovery.

content.value_statement: Marketing pages often fail when copy is vague or overclaims. This skill creates structured, honest copy with clear CTAs, alternatives, and testing guidance.
actual_capabilities: Gathers page purpose, audience, offer, proof, traffic source, and awareness level before writing.
Creates a copy brief summary and pauses for confirmation before drafting copy.
Writes labeled page sections, including headlines, subheadlines, CTAs, headers, and body copy.
Provides two to three headline and CTA alternatives with brief rationale.
Explains key copy choices and connects features to benefits and outcomes.
Recommends next-step testing when the copy is meant for experimentation.
limitations: It depends on accurate product, audience, and proof details from the user.
It will not fabricate statistics, testimonials, guarantees, or claims.
It does not replace legal, compliance, brand, or market research review.
It focuses on page copy and does not create full visual designs or analytics plans.

use_cases.title: Launch a Landing Page
use_cases.description: Create focused copy for a campaign page with one clear action and testable message hierarchy.

use_cases.title: Improve Product Messaging
use_cases.description: Turn feature lists into benefits, outcomes, objections, and proof-backed page sections.

use_cases.title: Refine Website Sections
use_cases.description: Rewrite homepage, pricing, feature, or about page copy for clarity, honesty, and better CTA alignment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Copy Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a new page copy project with basic context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write copy for a landing page. Ask for the missing details you need before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite Existing Page Copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page copy for clarity, claims, CTA alignment, and audience fit. Then rewrite it with a brief rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Create Headline and CTA Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three headline options and three CTA options for this page. Explain what each option is testing.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Conversion Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Draft a complete page after the copy brief is confirmed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the confirmed brief, write the full page copy with section labels, alternatives, annotations, and testing recommendations.

output_examples.input: A founder needs homepage copy for a scheduling tool aimed at small service businesses.
output: Copy Brief Summary: audience, page goal, value proposition, CTA, and awareness context.
Headline options focused on fewer missed bookings and faster scheduling.
Structured page copy with hero, benefits, proof placeholders, objections, and final CTA.

output_examples.input: A marketer wants to rewrite pricing page copy that feels vague and hard to compare.
output: Clear plan names and short descriptions tied to buyer needs.
CTA text that states the next step clearly.
FAQ copy that handles budget, setup, cancellation, and support objections.

output_examples.input: A product manager needs feature page copy for a new analytics dashboard.
output: Feature to benefit to outcome mapping for each section.
Page copy organized by headline, subheadline, benefits, proof, and CTA.
Testing ideas for headline clarity and CTA intent.

best_practices: Provide audience, offer, proof, objections, traffic source, and the primary CTA before drafting.
Confirm the copy brief before asking for final page copy.
Review every claim for proof, clarity, and compliance before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent testimonials, numbers, guarantees, or customer results.
Do not combine several page goals into one primary CTA.
Do not skip brief confirmation when audience or offer details are uncertain.

faq.question: What kinds of pages can this skill help with?
faq.answer: It supports homepages, landing pages, pricing pages, feature pages, product pages, and about pages.

faq.question: Does it write copy without asking questions?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to gather context and confirm a copy brief before drafting.

faq.question: Can it create proof points or testimonials?
faq.answer: No. It can use provided proof or mark placeholders, but it must not fabricate claims.

faq.question: Does it provide copy variants?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides two to three headline and primary CTA options with rationale.

faq.question: Can it support A/B testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It writes isolated messages and recommends next-step tests when experimentation is relevant.

faq.question: Is this a design or page builder skill?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on copy structure, messaging, CTAs, and annotations for review.
